display_name: List Session Ledger Events By Source Window
description:
Cycle 4b D14b — model-discoverable diagnostic verb that lists `__event` rows for a source kind / vendor in an optional `event_at` time window without a content-text predicate, so callers can list a source kind's recent events without a search term. SQL-lockdown Slice 7 (Architect-ruled denormalize): retired the former 3-table JOIN (event → session → source) onto a single-table `query_ordered` read over `__event` using the `session_vendor` + `source_kind` columns denormalized onto each event at append time (faithful-forever — both INSERT-only on their source rows, events never re-parented; pre-migration rows are filled once via `backfill_event_source_denormalization`).

W5.E §5.5 G5 signature relaxation: `source_kind`, `since`, and `until` are all now optional. Callers MUST supply at least one of `source_kind` / `vendor` — unbounded ledger scans are not the verb's contract; the service raises `ValueError` on neither. When `until` is omitted it defaults to `datetime.now(UTC)` at the service-layer entry so vendor-/source_kind-only audit pulls return the most recent events without an explicit upper bound. The existing triple-positional call shape `list_events_by_source_window(source_kind, since, until)` keeps working unchanged.

When to use. (a) Recent-activity probes: "what events did `chatgpt_export` land in the last hour?" (b) Re-walk validation: after `reset_source_cursor` + `trigger_poll`, list events with `since` set to the re-walk start time and confirm they cover the expected range. (c) Cross-vendor source comparisons: same `[since, until]` window across two source kinds to see relative throughput. (d) **Vendor-only audit pull (W5.E §5.5)**: supply `vendor='codex'` alone (no source_kind, no time window) to pull the most-recent events across ALL codex source_kinds (`codex_local + codex_history + codex_state + codex_goals + codex_memories + codex_ambient + codex_pushed`) combined.

Returns events ordered by `event_at DESC` (newest first), bounded by `limit` (clamped to `[1, 100]` — SQL-lockdown Slice 7 narrowed the former 200 to the `query_ordered` ≤100 cap; page via `until` for longer spans). Per-row envelope: `{event_id, session_id, sequence, event_at (ISO), role, content_text, vendor, source_kind}`. Both `vendor` (the `session_vendor` column) and `source_kind` ride denormalized `__event` columns, so the filter is a single-table read — no JOIN.

This verb returns events ordered strictly by event_at within the window with NO content-text predicate; use it when you don't have a search term.

This verb is `is_discoverable=true` — model can find it via `process_search` and proposes it for source/window queries.
embedding_description: List __event rows for one IngestSourceKind and/or SourceVendor in optional [since, until] event_at window. Returns events event_at DESC bounded by limit (1..100). Single-table read over __event (denormalized session_vendor + source_kind columns); NO content-text predicate, NO JOIN. Use for recent-activity probes, re-walk validation after reset_source_cursor, cross-source throughput, vendor-only audit pulls.

result_processor_customizations.action_label: List Session Ledger Events By Source Window
result_processor_customizations.result_description: Per-row envelope: `{event_id, session_id, sequence, event_at (ISO-8601), role, content_text, vendor, source_kind}`. Ordering: `event_at DESC` (newest first). Bounded by `limit` (default 20, max 100).
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: Use the returned `event_id` + `session_id` to drill into per-event detail via `get_session_timeline`. For aggregate counts, narrow the window and re-issue rather than paginating — this verb has no cursor / offset support by design.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Single-table `query_ordered` over `__event` filtered by the denormalized `source_kind` + `session_vendor` columns + an `event_at <= until` upper bound (the `since` lower bound is a Python post-filter on the page). SQL-lockdown Slice 7 retired the former 3-table JOIN.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: LedgerRepositoryError: the SELECT failed. Common causes: malformed ISO-8601 `since`/`until` strings (must be timezone-aware), unknown `source_kind` value (must be an `IngestSourceKind` StrEnum value), state_service unavailable.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: Confirm `since` and `until` parse as timezone-aware ISO-8601 (e.g. `2026-06-13T00:00:00+00:00`). Confirm `source_kind` is one of the known `IngestSourceKind` values via `list_sources` (which carries `source_kind` per row). Confirm `state_service` is responsive via `list_sources`. Re-run.
